why: The C12 relaxation made the model more willing to place cuts after determiners/short prepositions, which produced more earlier/single‑word-ish cuts and harmed the smallest latency bins (≤3, ≤5); the inserted C7 rule pushed the model away from cuts that end inside subordinate/verb‑final clauses, which slightly improved mid/longer bins (≤7, ≤10). The two edits offset each other so the net H_set change is near zero but with small harms concentrated in short‑latency settings.
lesson: Respect the binwise tradeoff: keep permissive cuts that help very short latencies only insofar as they don't create isolated verb/auxiliary or other head‑detaching cuts, while retaining the clause‑final protection for true subordinate/verb‑final fragments.
